title: Localization equivalence from an idempotent kernel
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, S an R-algebra, and s:S→R an R-algebra homomorphism. Let e in S be idempotent, s(e)=1, and ker(s)=(1-e)S. There is an R-algebra equivalence S[1/e]≅R sending x/1 to s(x) for every x in S.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), first paragraph: 'the surjective ring map $A'/IA'\to A/I$ is etale by Algebra, Lemma 00U7 (lemma-map-between-etale) and then we get the desired idempotent by Algebra, Lemma 00U8 (lemma-surjective-flat-finitely-presented)' (literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex); used without comment in the proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): '$B'/IB'=A/I\times C$'

proof.text:
Proof: Give R its S-algebra structure through s. Since s(e)=1, each r is the
image of e*algebraMap R S r, so this algebra map is surjective. Its kernel is
(1-e), and e is idempotent. The Mathlib criterion
IsLocalization.away_of_isIdempotentElem therefore makes R a localization of S
away from e. Uniqueness of localization gives an S-algebra equivalence from
Localization.Away e to R, which sends the image of x to s(x). Its underlying
ring equivalence is an R-algebra equivalence: on an R-scalar r, the scalar-tower
formula expresses its image as the image of algebraMap R S r, and s sends that
element to r. This proves both the equivalence and the required extension formula.

lean.statement: theorem exists_localization_equiv_of_idempotent {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (s : S →ₐ[R] R) (e : S) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (hse : s e = 1) (hker : RingHom.ker s.toRingHom = Ideal.span {1 - e}) : ∃ ψ : Localization.Away e ≃ₐ[R] R, ∀ x : S, ψ (algebraMap S (Localization.Away e) x) = s x
